exposure: maternal obesity (BMI class I, II, and III)
outcome: adverse maternal outcomes (hypertension, pregestational diabetes, severe preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, cesarean delivery)
adverse neonatal outcomes (respiratory distress syndrome, neonatal intensive care unit admission, fetal anomalies, sepsis)
cohort: The study included 58,497 singleton pregnancies delivered between 24 and 42 weeks gestation at an urban county hospital between 2013 and 2021 in a Hispanic population, categorized by maternal BMI.
finding: Increasing maternal body mass index is associated with a significant dose-dependent increase in multiple adverse perinatal outcomes, including severe preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, cesarean delivery, and increased neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Higher maternal BMI was associated with a significant dose-dependent increase in cesarean delivery rates.
